subject: SCCs module execution pathway — HealthTech: recommended module and timeline
messages:
From: Emma Stevens <emma.stevens@healthtech.sol>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@healthtech.sol>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SCCs — module preference and evidence for HealthTech POC

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal has asked us to confirm the preferred execution path for cross-border transfers between the EU and the UK for the pilot. Our privacy lead needs to know which SCC module Redwood recommends so we can align our DPA scope and internal DPIA.

Can you:
- Confirm which SCC modules Redwood recommends for a cloud-hosted hosted inference deployment (no on-prem data residency requirement).
- Share the minimum evidence we should expect to provide (SOC 2 excerpt, processor mix, IP allowlist, CSV of retained logs).
- Give an estimated timeline for execution if we go with Drafting Option A (Redwood provides standard UK addendum + DPA redlines).

I've attached the checklist we started. If easier, we can schedule a short call with your security team.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Stevens
Head of Privacy Operations
HealthTech Solutions
Attachment: SCCs-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Stevens <emma.stevens@healthtech.sol>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCCs — module preference and evidence for HealthTech POC

Hi Emma — appreciated the follow-up and the checklist. Short answers up front:
- Recommendation: For the configuration you described (Redwood hosted inference, controlled customer data flows), we commonly execute Module 2 for EU->UK transfers when the UK recipient is a processor acting under your instructions, accompanied by the standard UK Addendum. For EU->third countries under EU SCCs, Module 1 (controller->processor) is usually the baseline but with the UK-specific pathway we prefer the UK Addendum + Module 2 to avoid duplication for UK transfers.
- Evidence: minimum set is SOC 2 Type II summary (security controls), network architecture diagram (showing VPC, ingress/egress controls), key management statement (KMS/HSM usage), and an operations runbook excerpt showing retention and KV cache behavior. The SOC excerpt and architecture diagram are most commonly requested.
- Timeline: if you accept our standard DPA + UK Addendum with no bespoke legal carve-outs, we can route signatures and complete in ~7-10 business days. If you need contract redlines or additional security attestations, plan for 3-4 weeks.

I'll loop in Soojin (legal) and Neha (security/compliance) to call out any required evidence we should expect and to confirm whether Module 2 is safe for both EU and UK legs in your exact flow.

Next steps: Soojin — can you confirm whether we need to offer a combined EU SCCs Module 1/2 option, or if the UK Addendum + Module 2 is sufficient for HealthTech's use case? Also flag anything in the attached DPA redlines that would change our timeline.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Stevens <emma.stevens@healthtech.sol>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCCs — module preference and evidence for HealthTech POC

Marcus / Emma — copying in the narrow legal treatment below to keep things operationally useful. This is a quick summary, not full legal advice: 

- UK transfers: For processor relationships where the UK entity is performing processing on behalf of the EU controller, the UK Addendum paired with EU SCCs Module 2 is our pragmatic default. It minimizes dual-signature friction for UK companies without requiring the controller->processor Module 1 path in every case.
- EU -> third country (non-UK): If transfers go direct to Redwood infrastructure in a non-EEA region (e.g., US cloud region), then the EU SCCs Module 1 (controller->processor) + Module 2 (processor->sub-processor) mapping must be evaluated. In practice, we often rely on Module 1 executed between customer (controller) and Redwood (processor), with internal processor mappings documented.

Evidence list (what we'll ask HealthTech to provide):
1) SOC 2 Type II executive summary (PDF)
2) Network architecture diagram (PDF/PNG)
3) A short statement on regulated data types and any HIPAA applicability
4) List of sub-processor regions (CSV)

We can provide:
- Redwood's standard UK Addendum template and our DPA redline (attached).
- A pre-filled DocuSign package for fast execution.

If HealthTech requires an alternative (for example, Module 1 end-to-end mapping because of controller obligations), flag that ASAP — it will add review time.

Attachment: DPA-redline-v1.docx (for Marcus: note the liability cap clause we expect to negotiate)

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Stevens <emma.stevens@healthtech.sol>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCCs — module preference and evidence for HealthTech POC

Quick operational clarifications from security:
- SOC 2: we typically share the public SOC 2 summary + specific control mappings on request. We do not share the full report until an NDA or written request is in place, but we can provide the sections that address access control, encryption at rest/in transit, and incident response.
- Logs & retention: default retention for inference logs is 30 days unless you opt into extended retention (enterprise seat). We can provide a CSV with retention buckets and log types for your DPIA.
- KMS: we use customer-managed keys for Dedicated customers; for hosted customers we offer HSM-backed KMS in supported regions — include region preference in your response and we'll list options.

If HealthTech confirms they are processing health data subject to HIPAA, we will add the HIPAA appendix and require a business associate agreement. That will change the negotiation path and likely the timeline (expect +2 weeks).

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Stevens <emma.stevens@healthtech.sol>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCCs — module preference and evidence for HealthTech POC

Emma — thanks for the patience. Based on our internal alignment:
- Recommended path: accept Redwood DPA + UK Addendum with Module 2 mapping for the UK leg; execute EU SCCs Module 1 (customer -> Redwood) for any transfers to non-EEA cloud regions, documented in Schedule A. This hybrid avoids dual-contract friction while preserving clear controller->processor responsibility where required.
- Please confirm whether HealthTech will be providing HIPAA applicability confirmation. If "yes", we will add the BAA/HIPAA appendix and the timeline shifts to ~3-4 weeks.
- Action items for HealthTech to keep to the ~7-10 business day timeline:
  1) Return signed DPA redline acceptance or a short list of top 3 redlines to negotiate.
  2) Provide SOC 2 executive summary and network diagram.
  3) Confirm region preference for KMS (EU only / EU + US / Dedicated).

If you want, I'll drop a pre-filled DocuSign link and our UK Addendum so legal can sign immediately.

Best regards,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
